question: Why does an operating system use paging instead of contiguous allocation?

beats.speaker: interviewer
beats.line: Why does an operating system use paging instead of contiguous allocation?

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: Contiguous allocation forces every process to occupy one unbroken block of physical memory.
beats.source_quote: Contiguous allocation forces every process to occupy one unbroken block of physical memory.

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: Over time that produces external fragmentation, where enough free memory exists but no single block is large enough.
beats.source_quote: Over time this produces external fragmentation: enough total free memory exists, but no single block is large enough.

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: Paging removes that requirement by dividing memory into fixed-size frames and the address space into pages.
beats.source_quote: Paging removes the requirement for contiguity.

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: So any page may be placed in any free frame, and the gaps become usable.
beats.source_quote: Any page may be placed in any free frame.
